recents.title: PhoenixOS was Presented at ChinaSys'24 Fall
recents.description:
Prof. Xingda Wei and I presented PhoenixOS in the talk session of ChinaSys'24.

I am also glad to directly discuss with authors of below excellent works:

  • Vsync [ASPLOS'21]: a framework to assist in optimizing and verifying synchronization primitives on WMM architectures.
  • HCache [EuroSys'25]: restore LLM states from intermediate activations and thus utilize computational and I/O resources with low overhead.
  • T-MAC: a kernel library to directly support mixed-precision matrix multiplication (int1/2/3/4 x int8/fp16/fp32) without the need for dequantization by utilizing lookup tables;
  • Rubick: a cluster scheduling system for deep learning training that exploits the reconfigurability to improve job performance and cluster efficiency.
  • ...

recents.title: Project PhoenixOS is Open Sourced!
recents.description:
PhoenixOS is the first OS-level system to support Checkpoint / Restore (C/R) GPU program without requiring the GPU program to stop, which is a key feature to support fast live-migration, restore of GPU program. Welcome to use PhoenixOS, more details are disclosed in our arXiv paper.

This project is done while I was doing research intern at IPADS, Shanghai Jiaotong University. This project is advised by Prof. Xingda Wei.

recents.title: Won <font color="red">National First Prize</font> at NECSDC!
recents.description:
I led a team won the 2022 National First Prize at National Embedded Chip and System Design Competition (NECSDC)! Congratulate to all my teammates!

Our team designed and implemented a face tracing conference system based on mobile chip from HiSilicon, with the help of reinforcement leanrnig (RL) for arm controling and YoLo-v5 for face identifying.

Please check the technical report above to learn what we have done.
